sections.html:
Two offices handle property tax here. The Tax Commissioner, at 324 East Pine Street in Fitzgerald, takes care of bills and payments. What a property is worth is the Board of Tax Assessors' call. The commissioner's number is (229) 426-5144, answered on weekdays, and the counter stays staffed until half past four. The assessors are at (229) 426-5147.

A payment, a lien or a wrong mailing address is a commissioner matter. A value, a homestead file or an exemption belongs with the assessors. Appraisers keep inspecting properties, stop at every parcel with a building permit, and look for a current decal on each mobile home.

  • Tax Commissioner: statements, receipts, liens, online payments
  • Board of Tax Assessors: value, returns, exemptions, notices of assessment
  • Clerk of Superior Court: your warranty deed copy, from the courthouse deed room

sections.h2: Ben Hill County at a glance
sections.html:
This is a small south Georgia county. Fitzgerald is its only city and also the seat. The population slipped from 17,194 at the 2020 census to an estimate of 17,099 for 2025. A typical home is valued at $112,700 while a typical household earns $41,758, so a tax bill takes a bigger bite here than in a pricier market.

Housing totals 8,166 units in 2025, and owners occupy 63.3 percent. Middle gross rent is $688 a month and the average commute is only 16.8 minutes. Buyers at these price levels watch every dollar. Clear any tax question before you list, and keep a recent paid receipt handy for a buyer who asks.

Land, houses and business personal property are normally due December 1. Georgia's default is December 20 and counties are allowed to move it, which is why the day on your own statement is the one to follow. Mobile homes are due April 1, and a call to the office will confirm that for your account.

Late accounts pay 1% interest a month. Once 90 days go by, a one-time 10% penalty applies, though a homesteaded parcel owing under $500 escapes it. Beyond 90 days the balance can become a FiFa lien filed with the Clerk of Superior Court, which credit bureaus may see, and the commissioner is then free to levy on the parcel.

The owner receives the statement, never the lender. When escrow covers your tax, forward the bill or verify that the servicer is paying.

At the counter, cash and checks add no charge, and mailing a check is fine as well. The county's GovtWindow portal takes online payments, and PayPal and cards are offered only on the website. The convenience charge for each online method appears before you confirm, which leaves you free to back out and pay by check.

  • In person: 324 East Pine Street, Fitzgerald, Georgia 31750
  • By phone for questions: (229) 426-5144
  • Portal help line: (877) 575-7233

You qualify by owning and occupying the home on January 1, with your application in the assessors' hands before April 1. Once granted, it continues yearly while you stay. A move calls for a fresh application at the new address, and a late filing just pushes the benefit out a year.

An owner who reaches 62 may apply for an additional exemption. Business inventory can earn a freeport exemption where local voters have approved one. Local legislation can raise the base amounts, so call the assessors for the dollar figure that applies to you.

If you are selling, your exemption does not travel with the house. The buyer files a new application, and telling their agent early avoids a surprise on the first bill.

sections.h2: How values are set and challenged
sections.html:
From winter into early spring, up to April 1, you can file a return stating your own value. If the board sees it differently, it mails a notice with its number. Taxable value equals 40% of market value, and a mill is one dollar for every $1,000 of it.

Appeal within 45 days of the notice date. Your case then goes to the county Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator. If the outcome still bothers you, deliver written notice to the assessors and move on to superior court. A claim for tax charged by mistake must be made within three years of payment.

Before you appeal, ask the assessors what comparable sales they used and compare your house with those. Photos of problems, such as a failing roof or an unfinished room, back up a lower value. Keep a copy of whatever you deliver and note the date, because the clock starts on the notice date and not on the day you open the envelope.

Know the balance and the billed owner before you sign. A statement is addressed to the January 1 owner, so it may bear your name even when the deed passes to the buyer later in the year. Get a printed balance from the commissioner and ask the closing agent how the year is shared.

A lien stands in the way of clean title. Sellers mostly clear it out of the sale money, wiring the commissioner's payoff figure. A house that needs repairs can still sell while taxes are owed, and that is one reason some owners go with a cash buyer who accepts it as is.

At the counter on East Pine Street, bring your deed or parcel number, your latest statement and any lien notice. Ask for the payoff in writing with its good-through date, because interest builds each month.

In Georgia a mobile or modular home is personal property. Its owner files a return and obtains a location permit every year, and the permit waits until the whole tax is paid. April 1 is the due date for that account, so confirm the date on yours with the commissioner.

Assessors look for a current decal when they inspect. If you sell one, the next owner takes over the paperwork trail, so pay the tax and settle the permit before the handoff and keep the paid receipt.

Owners who moved without updating an address should ask the assessors whether mail came back undelivered, so future notices reach the right place. A missed notice does not stop the 45-day appeal clock.

If you inherited a mobile home or bought one without the paperwork, ask the commissioner what is on file before you list it. A clean permit history makes the sale simpler, and a buyer or lender will usually ask for proof that the tax is current.

faqs.q: When is real estate tax due in Ben Hill County?
faqs.a: Most bills are due December 1, but the date printed on your statement controls. Call (229) 426-5144 to confirm.

faqs.q: What does a late Ben Hill County payment cost?
faqs.a: Interest runs 1% per month, and a 10% penalty is added after 90 days. Homesteaded property with a liability under $500 skips the penalty.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for homestead exemption in Ben Hill County?
faqs.a: Apply with the Tax Assessor, and make sure the paperwork arrives before April 1. You must own the home and live there on January 1.

faqs.q: What is the appeal window in Ben Hill County?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice date. Appeals go to the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, with superior court after that.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Ben Hill County taxes without a fee?
faqs.a: Yes. Paying cash or check at the counter or mailing a check costs nothing extra, while online payments add a convenience charge.
